_note: PRD v5 R9: YouTube research and production planning (`ca youtube`, skill make-youtube). Separate from the social workflow; shares only the registry (BG IDs, approval), storage, tracker and authorization layers. Roman records, the editing agency (Takwa) edits; the system never renders a video. Formula: config/formulas.json youtube_longform (the 8-step storytelling formula, R9.6). Length: formats.long.targetWords (about 12 minutes, 1,600-1,800 spoken German words) and formats.short.targetWords (about 1 minute, 140-160 words), at wordsPerMinute; a script outside it is a warning, not an error, until Roman confirms Q4.
_topicsPerMonthNote: PRD v6 weekly (2026-10-22): the monthly count per format is config/deliverables.json weeklySet.youtube x monthMultiplier (long 8, short 16); topicsPerMonth is the fallback for long-form only.

editorialFocus._note: Persistent editorial preference; monthly capacity and approval gates remain unchanged.
priorityThemes: situations where AI appears out of control
harm caused by incorrect AI use
documented German problems AI could help solve
avoidUnlessRequested: business growth topics without a documented German societal problem
editorialFocus.sourceRule: Use current, opened sources and do not claim AI will solve a problem unless the evidence supports it.

_wordsPerMinuteNote: PRD Phase 2 P2-R5: the speaking pace for the length and the storyboard timings; ~130 until calibrated on Roman's real takes (words of a recorded script / its minutes). The length target stays targetWords.

formats._note: PRD v6 weekly §3-4: two independent script pipelines, chosen with `ca youtube plan --format short|long` (skill make-youtube: "make short video script", "make long video script"). Each has its own prompt, word target, presenter, folder layout and Drive folder. Deliverables are scripts only (no video, voice or host generation).

long.label: Long-form
long.structure: Strong hook (a real, sourced statistic, risk or finding, not sensational; what viewers can do) -> topic segments (news -> why it matters -> analysis and implications) with transitions -> short conclusion. Balanced: risks and positive developments.

short.label: Short-form

presenter.rule: Podcast-style dialogue: every paragraph starts with HOST: (the AI-generated host introduces and asks) or ROMAN: (Roman analyses); both speak.

short.structure: One topic; a strong hook in the first line; a natural ending (a takeaway, a question or a strong statement).

A.name: Investigativ
A.approach: Start with a real, documented incident; uncover its causes and consequences step by step, like an investigation; end with what companies and people should do now.

B.name: Direkte Warnung
B.approach: Start with the immediate risk or a direct question to the viewer; give the evidence quickly; spend the most time on the practical response.

C.name: Menschlich
C.approach: Start with a realistic everyday or workplace scenario, clearly framed as illustrative ("Stellen Sie sich vor ..."); tie it to the verified facts and end with solutions. Never present the scenario as a real event and never as something Roman experienced.

S.name: Dialog
S.approach: Short-form only: one style, no style subfolder. HOST opens with the hook as a question or a striking statement, ROMAN explains what it means for German companies, workers or society, HOST asks one follow-up, ROMAN ends with a takeaway, a question or a strong statement.

openingTypes._note: P2-R3/R4: how a script opens; the outline (research.txt section 12) names one per style, each style a different one. The difference check reads the first sentence: question (it ends with ?), scenario (an illustrativeMarker), quote (it starts with a quotation mark), else a statement (incident, statistic or contradiction: the outline decides).
openingTypes.incident: a documented case, told as it happened
openingTypes.question: a direct question to the viewer
openingTypes.scenario: an illustrative everyday scenario, framed as such (Stellen Sie sich vor ...)
openingTypes.statistic: one verified number and what it means
openingTypes.quote: an exact quotation from the research
openingTypes.contradiction: a common belief, then what the facts show

spoken._note: P2-R5 warnings of the teleprompter check (german-editorial references/german-style.md, Gesprochenes Deutsch): sentences over sentenceMaxWords words, symbols, brackets and slashes, written abbreviations, digits not written for speaking (numeric dates, ranges with a dash, a digit glued to a letter). Never blocking.

similarity._note: the free difference check between two styles: share of shared word trigrams in the openings and in the whole scripts; above the limit the pair is flagged as too similar. 2026-10-22 (P2-R4): also the same opening type (the first sentence, or the outline's when both are statements), the same order of the outline points (section 12 order) or of the facts the scripts use (at least minSameFactOrder facts), and the share of near-identical sentences (difflib ratio at least sentenceRatio) above maxSentenceOverlap

_treeNote: PRD v6 weekly §3-4, §6: long-form: outputs/YouTube Long-Form/<English Topic Title> <YYYY-MM-DD>/Style A|B|C/ (script-en-de.md, teleprompter-de.txt, storyboard.md); short-form: outputs/YouTube Short-Form/<English Topic Title> <YYYY-MM-DD>/ with the same 3 files directly (one style). research.txt stays local in the topic folder (the working file; never uploaded): every reference sits inline in storyboard.md, right after the scene it supports. The BG ID, titleEn and the rest of the metadata live in outputs/_system/youtube/<BG-ID>.json. A re-run reuses the folder and writes a changed file as <name>_v2 (never overwrites).
